## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible loop1 with branchless blend and per-particle hash RNG can approach the streaming bandwidth ceiling on this workload.

## Cache saturation
The smallest measured N=4000 already exceeds the L1d spill (N≈963), so the L1d→L2 transition is not directly observed. Cost FALLS sharply from N=4000 to N=16000 (11.759→8.139 ns/p at q=0.01), reflecting fixed-overhead amortization at small N. From N=16000 onward cost stays FLAT: at q=0.01, ns/p is 8.139 at N=16000, 7.989 at N=65000 (just past the L2 spill at N≈61680), and 7.946 at N=1M — no knee at the L2→DRAM transition. Death rate does not raise the floor; q=0.25 is marginally faster (7.666 vs 8.139 ns/p at N=16000), but the N-shape is identical across all death rates: overhead-dominated at N=4000, flat thereafter.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.87 GB/s at N=16000, q=0.25 — 35% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0.01 the peak is 8.56 GB/s (N=1M), ~34% of ceiling. Bandwidth is flat across N from 16000 onward and varies little with death rate (8.5–8.9 GB/s). The algorithm is compute/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: it never approaches the streaming ceiling, and the absence of any N-dependent rise rules out a bandwidth wall. The flat 35% profile across all regimes indicates the bottleneck is per-particle scalar work and scatter, not memory throughput.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the step body. Of 352 instructions, only 2 carry vector suffixes — both `movi.2d` for register zeroing, not computation. Loop1 is delegated to `bl _halide_b1` (not disassembled here); the visible code is the loop2 render loop, entirely scalar: `ldp s4, s5` and `ldr s16` for per-particle loads, scalar `fmul s4`, `fadd s4`, `fsub s4`, `fcvtzs` for coordinate conversion. Pixel writes use byte-granular `ldrb`/`strb` pairs (12 ldrb, 16 strb in the histogram) with `csel`-based clamping to 0xFF — a scatter that cannot stream. No gather (`ld1` indexed) and no SIMD arithmetic (`fmul.4s`) appear. The scalar render with byte stores explains why bandwidth stalls at 35% of ceiling regardless of N.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algorithm never exceeds 8.87 GB/s = 35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling, with only 2 vector instructions (both `movi.2d` zero-ops) and no SIMD arithmetic in the step body. The flat ns/p curve from N=16000 through the L2 spill (8.139→7.946 ns/p at q=0.01) confirms the bottleneck is scalar computation and byte-granular scatter in the render, not memory bandwidth, so the Halide-expressible loop1 cannot approach the streaming ceiling in this configuration.
